A bitmap as a sorted vector

Source: R/methods.R, R/wide.R
zuroar-vector.Rd

A bitmap behaves like sort(unique(v)) kept compressed. It is a vector to R: length() is the number of values, an integer, or a double above .Machine$integer.max, as for a long vector; x[[k]] is the k-th smallest value; x[i] is a bitmap of the values at positions i; head() and tail() return bitmaps; v %in% x and match(v, x) work by expanding x into a double vector first, so roar_contains() is the fast membership test. sum() adds the values in one pass. min(), max() and range() read the ends without expanding the bitmap; an empty bitmap has none, so they are errors there. as.double() returns every value exactly. as.integer() does too, and is an error when a value is above .Machine$integer.max, rather than giving NA. A bitmap can be a data-frame column, and survives saveRDS(), serialize() and a trip to another R process on its own. as.character() gives decimal text.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  nm = deparse1(substitute(x))
)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
mtfrm(x)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
Summary(..., na.rm = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
as.double(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
as.numeric(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
as.character(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
as.integer(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
format(x, n = 10, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
print(x, n = 10, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
length(x)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
Summary(..., na.rm = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
as.character(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
as.double(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
as.numeric(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
as.integer(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
format(x, n = 10, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
print(x, n = 10, ...)

Arguments

x

A bitmap.

row.names, optional, nm

As for as.data.frame.vector().

...

For Summary, further arguments, which must be absent. For the others, ignored or passed on.

na.rm

Ignored: a bitmap holds no NA.

n

For format() and print(), how many values to show.

Value

[ returns a bitmap. min() and max() return a single double (text for a zuroar64), range() two, sum() one, as.double() and as.integer() a vector, format() a string, print() x, invisibly, and as.data.frame() a data frame with one column.

Details

A zuroar64 has the same methods (see roar64()): min(), max() and range() return decimal text, as.double() is an error when a value is at or above 2^53, and length() is an error above 2^53. It is an external pointer, not a vector, so it does not survive saveRDS(), and %in%, match(), sum() and data-frame columns are not available for it.

The values are read from the compressed form on demand and never expanded behind your back: an operation that needs them as a plain vector, such as x[1] <- 5, identical(x, y) or cumsum(x), is a zuroar_error_unsupported error. Compare bitmaps as sets with ==, and expand one explicitly with as.double().

format() gives one line describing the bitmap, which print() shows. To loop over the values, use for (v in x) or lapply(x, f).

Examples

x <- roar(c(1, 5, 9, 100000))
length(x)
#> [1] 4
x[[2]]
#> [1] 5
x[2:3]
#> <zuroar> 2 values in [5, 9]: 5 9
c(5, 6) %in% x
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE
range(x)
#> [1] 1e+00 1e+05
as.integer(x)
#> [1]      1      5      9 100000
x
#> <zuroar> 4 values in [1, 100000]: 1 5 9 100000
